If you tried and missed out on tickets for Celine Dion's big Paris comeback, it's not too late.

All 16 of her September and October 2026 shows at Plenitude Arena, the venue known as Paris La Defense Arena until July, sold out within hours. Millions of fans entered the presale lottery, and many missed out.

The good news is it's all coming back to Paris, with 10 extra shows added for May 2027. The bad news? Standard tickets have all sold out too.

This is where the power of points comes in: As the official hotel partner of the residency, Marriott Bonvoy is offering members the opportunity to redeem points for exclusive concert packages through the Marriott Bonvoy Moments platform.

Here's how Marriott Bonvoy points can help you see this global icon light up the stage in the City of Lights next year.

Related: The best Marriott redemptions might not involve a hotel at all

Marriott has been releasing Bonvoy Moments experiences for Celine's May run of shows and plans to continue through the end of January 2027. The cheapest ticket-only auctions open at 20,000 Marriott Bonvoy points for a pair of Experience Privilege tickets, while hotel-and-hospitality packages start at 40,000 points. Those are opening bids, not fixed redemption prices, and final bids may be far higher.

These packages are an official, peace-of-mind route to tickets without taking the risks that can come with unauthorized resale websites, as The Points Guy founder Brian Kelly discovered firsthand.

The star of the show is the Ultimate Celine Dion Experience, which includes an exclusive backstage tour of Plenitude Arena, a VIP merchandise pack, two Salon Premium Hospitality tickets with hospitality access and Level 1 reserved seating, breakfast for two and a one-night stay in the "Paris, I'm Ready" Suite at Le Meridien Paris Arc de Triomphe.

Other Moments packages pair tickets with stays at Le Meridien Paris Arc de Triomphe, Renaissance Paris La Defense Hotel, Renaissance Paris Nobel Tour Eiffel Hotel, Renaissance Paris Republique Hotel and citizenM Paris La Defense.

The Renaissance Paris La Defense Hotel and citizenM Paris La Defense are both very close to the arena, so there's no need to drive all night to make the show.

If none of them appeal, here's where else you can stay in Paris on points.

Marriott also offered two 1-Point Drops for the 2027 shows on Oct. 28 and 29, each releasing four pairs of tickets for just 1 Marriott Bonvoy point. Missed them? Think twice before beating yourself up, as Marriott says the 2026 drops went in seconds.

Related: You might be able to get these exclusive music festival tickets for 1 Marriott Bonvoy point

Many of the remaining packages are auctions, which means taking chances on how high other fans will go. There are no set prices, so it's worth knowing that TPG values Marriott Bonvoy points at 0.75 cents each before you bid.

Here's how to get your bid in before the listings close:

Related: Marriott Bonvoy will now let you see where you stand in line for a hotel upgrade

I was able to experience the "Two Salon Premium Hospitality Tickets + citizenM stay" package. The citizenM Paris La Defense hotel could not be more convenient, being directly across from the Plenitude Arena where you can watch the crowds gather with a glass of Champagne in hand from the comfort of the hotel bar's balcony.

The rooms are fairly compact with the bed against the window, but many rooms offer spectacular views of the arena, or La Grande Arche, as mine did.

It was my first time staying at a citizenM property, and I loved the bright and colorful common spaces which were abuzz with Celine fans, sharing their excitement (and favorite songs) in advance of the big event.

Plenitude Arena is Europe's largest indoor arena. Celine's 16-show 2026 run drew 539,000 fans, an average of almost 33,700 per night. As a result, huge crowds left the arena at the same time after each show.

The convenience of being able to walk just a few hundred feet from the exit doors to the hotel's bar, which is reserved for in-house guests after each concert and bask in the afterglow of the concert with a celebratory beverage while avoiding the hordes outside was terrific.

While attendees with regular seats queued all the way up to La Grande Arche to enter the arena, the Salon Hospitality tickets included express entry at Gate 21.

We were through security and into a secret VIP entrance in two minutes, before boarding a private escalator upstairs.

From there it was straight into a large hospitality suite with an open bar serving Champagne, wine, beer, spirits and soft drinks.

There was also a selection of canapes available before the show started.

I was a little surprised to hear the staff advise that the hospitality was only available until the show started, having recently enjoyed five hours of hospitality suite indulgence at a World of Hyatt redemption experience.

They explained that this was a specific condition set by Celine's management, and that all food and beverage outlets inside the venue closed when the show started each night.

As the lights dimmed, we walked down to our seats.

I expected the Plenitude Arena to be large, but even I was surprised by its scale.

This ticket package included reserved seats midway up the lower bowl to the side of the stage, an excellent vantage point. Given how far back the floor seats go and that the stage isn't overly high, these seats, raised just enough to give an excellent view of the stage and arena, seemed much better than the rear floor seats.

While Marriott does not publish a cash value for the auction packages, to give you an idea of how good these seats are, Plenitude Arena sold similar Salon Premium Hospitality Tickets for just over $1,000 each for October's shows.

Celine came on around 9 p.m. and belted out the hits over the next two hours (there was no support act).

I won't give away too much, beyond saying that although a lot of the songs are in French — she is the best-selling French-language artist in history, and I was in Paris after all — all her iconic English-language hits are in there, as well as a few surprises.

I shed more than a few tears, particularly during "Because You Loved Me." To see an icon return to the stage after a long health battle with the rare autoimmune neurological disorder stiff-person syndrome was truly inspiring.

If you’re looking to earn Marriott Bonvoy points, the following Marriott cards are currently offering strong welcome bonuses:

You can also transfer Bilt Points, Chase Ultimate Rewards points and American Express Membership Rewards points to Marriott Bonvoy at a 1:1 ratio. American Express is currently offering a 35% transfer bonus to Marriott Bonvoy through Dec. 10, meaning 1,000 Membership Rewards points become 1,350 Marriott Bonvoy points.

In our experience, points transfer almost instantly from all these programs.

If you weren't lucky enough to secure one of the exception 1-Point Drops, you'll need to part with more Bonvoy points than that. Marriott doesn't publish retail prices for the auctions, and the value varies depending on whether a hotel stay is included, the type of concert tickets and other factors.

Based on my calculations, the package I experienced would retail for around $2,400, noting that all Standard tickets for next year's show are already sold out, which may drive up resale prices. Based on TPG's November 2026 valuation of Bonvoy points, that's about 320,000 points worth.

So, if you can get a similar package for that number of Bonvoy points or fewer, it's a great deal.

Marriott Bonvoy Moments offers a great opportunity for anyone who missed out on buying face-value tickets to Celine Dion's concert next year.

The opening bids are just that — opening bids — so decide what the experience is worth to you before entering an auction. Read the terms carefully, confirm you can travel on the fixed dates and remember that most packages do not include transportation.

Having experienced Salon Premium hospitality and stayed directly across from Plenitude Arena, I can say the hotel-and-hospitality packages offer much more than a great seat at the show. Marriott plans to release Moments through the end of January 2027, so fans who thought they had missed their chance should keep checking.

Alaska Atmos Rewards offers the Global Getaways promotion, whereby members can save on award tickets in select regions. Atmos Rewards launches this promotion on the first Wednesday of each month (which the program calls “Atmos Members Day”), so we just saw the one for November launched.

Let’s go over the opportunities, as you can save up to 50% on award tickets. There are some cool markets in which you can save miles, though unfortunately only economy travel qualifies.

For the new Alaska Atmos Rewards Global Getaways promotion, you can save up to 50% on award travel to nine destinations, with the following restrictions:

I very much appreciate Alaska Atmos Rewards’ creativity with this promotion, as nowadays it’s pretty rare to see programs offer award sales that are also valid for travel on partner airlines. #6159. KLM Plans 1,000 More Job Cuts

KLM expects to eliminate approximately 1,000 positions through productivity improvements as part of a restructuring announced Thursday.

The Dutch carrier said it would seek to limit the impact through natural attrition, voluntary arrangements and transfers. Other changes include moving about 800 ground services positions to outside providers and transferring 2,000 positions to Air France-KLM, including 1,500 at customer contact center Cygnific.

“But KLM’s future is not guaranteed,” CEO Marjan Rintel said in a statement, citing global instability, high fuel prices, and pressure on the industry.

KLM is targeting a structural productivity increase of at least 8% by 2028, alongside restrained wage growth. It said an additional €1 billion in annual earnings improvement is needed to fund investments.

The changes also affect its European fleet. KLM will replace planned Airbus A320s with Embraer E195-E2s, giving regional subsidiary Cityhopper a larger role. The A321neo will remain, while Boeing 737s and Embraer E190s will be phased out.

The announcement came as KLM reported a third-quarter operating profit of €458 million, up from €352 million a year earlier. For the first nine months of 2026, operating profit reached €526 million on revenue of €10.9 billion.

Despite the improvement, KLM said profitability remains insufficient to support its investment needs. Higher fuel costs and Middle East flight cancellations weighed on its passenger business, while Transavia faced competition and operational challenges.

“We need to increase it to more than 8% to secure a financially healthy future for KLM,” Chief Financial Officer Bas Brouns said of the airline’s profit margin.

#6158. Alaska, Mississippi Senate races separated by razor-thin vote margins

Former DOJ chief of staff Chad Mizelle weighs in on the highly contested Alaska Senate race between Mary Peltola and Dan Sullivan. Mizelle also analyzes the potential future of the Supreme Court following reports that Justice Samuel Alito does not plan to retire immediately.

Races between the candidates for U.S. Senate in Alaska and Mississippi are separated by razor-thin margins days after polls closed in the crucial midterm elections.

In Mississippi, where 95.6% of the votes have been counted, according to the Associated Press, Democratic candidate Scott Colom leads incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., 464,926 votes to 463,788, as of Thursday morning.

In Alaska, former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola, leads incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, by less than 700 votes.

DOJ SET TO APPEAL RULING IN ALASKA SENATE RACE DISPUTE OVER ‘DECOY DAN’

While Alaska still has a quarter of its votes to count, according to the AP, if the gap between Peltola and Sullivan remains this slim, the introduction of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan will loom large in post-election analyses.

Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, and former Rep. Mary Peltola, a Democrat from Alaska and U.S. Senate candidate, raise paddles during the 2026 Alaska Fisheries Debate in Kodiak, Alaska, on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. (Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

In July, the U.S. Justice Department opened an investigation into Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher who entered the Senate race in May.

TRUMP PROSECUTIONS UNDER BIDEN SET PRECEDENT FOR DOJ’S ALASKA ‘DECOY DAN’ PROBE, EX-FEC CHAIR SAYS

An October report from The New York Times said Daniel J. Sullivan had met with Democratic operatives and members of Peltola's campaign staff to encourage him to run. Peltola has denied any involvement in the scheme.

One voter interviewed after he cast his ballot Tuesday revealed that he believed he accidentally voted for the wrong Dan Sullivan.

MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT

"I don't remember seeing the other Dan Sullivan, I totally forgot to look for two Dan Sullivans," the bewildered voter revealed. "I definitely intended to vote for the real Dan Sullivan."

As of Thursday morning, Daniel J. Sullivan, aka "Decoy Dan," had garnered 3,600 votes from Alaskans, a number that's more than five times larger than the 637-vote margin separating Sen. Sullivan and Peltola.

PELTOLA CAMPAIGN'S ALLEGED DAN SULLIVAN SPOILER PLOT TAKES NEW TURN AS DOJ FACES MAJOR LEGAL HURDLE

Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, and former Rep. Mary Peltola, D-Alaska. (Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images | Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Under Alaska's ranked choice voting system, if no candidate achieves a 50% share of the vote, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and voters who chose that candidate first will have their votes redirected to their second choice.

President Donald Trump weighed in on the saga, demanding Daniel J. Sullivan's votes be given to Sen. Sullivan.

"The vote totals for the Fake Dan Sullivan, plus the other 'slug' that the Dems put on the Ballot, should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan, and the Election is over - He easily wins," Trump wrote in a Thursday morning post on Truth Social.

"There is no other fair solution! President DJT" he concluded.

GOVERNOR PROBING 'DECOY DAN' SULLIVAN ELECTION SCANDAL WARNS SYSTEM FLAW HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

Mary Peltola launches her campaign as a Democratic candidate for Senate in Anchorage, Alaska, on Jan. 17, 2026. (Reuters)

In Mississippi, officials are still waiting to receive a batch of 3,600 mail-in ballots, according to a statement from Secretary of State Michael Watson. The state allows mail-in ballots to be counted if they're received within five business days of the election, provided they were postmarked with a date of the election day or earlier.

NBC News' Decision Desk pegs the remaining ballots to be counted at 45,000.

TIM SCOTT DECLARES ALLEGED 'DECOY DAN' PLOT A 'CRIMINAL OFFENSE' AS DOJ INVESTIGATION ROCKS ALASKA

Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., clinched the GOP Senate nomination in Mississippi as she eyes a second term in the upper chamber. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Mississippi has no formal process for recounts, making a legal fight over the results increasingly likely.

"We will protect the process of this election, we'll protect the integrity of this election," Colom told reporters Wednesday, adding that he had "an army of lawyers" preparing for a court battle, Mississippi Public Broadcasting reported.

ALASKA'S GOVERNOR ORDERS INVESTIGATION AFTER NYT REPORT ON ALLEGED DEM-LINKED SENATE ELECTION SCHEME

Hyde-Smith's team, meanwhile, remains assured that the sitting senator will prevail.

"Our campaign is closely monitoring the remaining count," campaign manager Scott Monssen told MPB in a statement. "We remain confident that when every legally cast vote is fully and accurately counted, Mississippians will have reelected Cindy Hyde-Smith," he concluded.

#6157. Breeze Airways Launches 15 New Routes From Major Airport: See Full List Now

Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America. Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand. His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

One of the newest commercial airlines in the United States, Breeze Airways, since its inception in 2021, has quickly developed an extensive network of secondary routes across the country. The Utah-based low-cost carrier primarily operates on routes with no competition, focusing on secondary airports and bypassing the big, dominated hubs.

Breeze is adding a total of 15 routes from Raleigh–Durham International Airport (RDU) between May 2026 and June 2027, as the airline continues to develop its network. The airline operates a fleet of more than 60 Airbus A220-300 aircraft.

Breeze has rapidly expanded its reach from Raleigh-Durham, and the airport has quickly risen to become the airline's busiest airport with weekly departures. The airline, this November alone, will operate an average of 162 weekly departures, making the airline the fifth busiest at the North Carolina airport.

Raleigh has become a top-performing destination for the carrier, with the airline's Chief Executive Officer David Neeleman describing strong, consistent passenger demand and high load factors. This has resulted in the airline continuing to expand its reach from the airport, with 15 new routes.

In this list, Breeze adds 13 new domestic services, while two new international routes take flight, which include the popular tourist destination of Punta Cana International Airport (PUJ) in the Dominican Republic, and Nassau (NAS) in the Bahamas in time for next summer. The international services are detailed in the table above.

Taking into consideration the route to Punta Cana, May this year was the airline's biggest month for new routes from Raleigh. The airline added six additional domestic links, reaching as far as California, Florida, Maine, New York, Texas, and Wisconsin.

Part of this May expansion saw the carrier add Bangor International Airport (BGR), Madison (MSN), Newburgh / Stewart (SWF), San Antonio International Airport (SAT), Santa Ana / Orange County (SNA), and Vero Beach (VRB). No other airline competes with Breeze Airways directly on any of these routes, further highlighting the airline's dominance when serving secondary cities and airports.

In June, Breeze added its own service from Raleigh to Atlantic City International Airport (ACY). In July, this was followed by nonstop flights to Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport (BHM) and Tallahassee (TLH).

The airline has ended the only international route from Providence, while exited multiple underperforming domestic markets.

As the airline continues to push its dominance at Raleigh, in October, Breeze added a nonstop link to its hometown of Provo (PVU) in Utah. This will be followed by a service to James M Cox Dayton International Airport (DAY) in Ohio this November.

Over the winter, as seasonal services taper back for the cooler months, the airline will not relaunch a new route until June next year. In June 2027, Breeze plans to add three new links from Raleigh, including Nassau in the sun-soaked Bahamas. This new international service will then be complemented by Buffalo Niagara International Airport (BUF) and Las Vegas (LAS), which will then take flight.

Delta Air Lines, Frontier Airlines, Southwest Airlines

As already mentioned, Raleigh is Breeze's largest airport by weekly departures, ahead of close rivals Orlando International Airport (MCO) and Tampa International Airport (TPA). These are the only three current airports in the airline's network to register more than 100 weekly departing flights.

#6156. Teamsters Sue Horizon Air Over Pilot Rest Rules

The Teamsters have sued Horizon Air, alleging the Alaska Air Group subsidiary violated federal labor law by changing how it handles pilots who report fatigue.

The Teamsters Airline Division and Local 1224 filed the lawsuit Oct. 23 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington. The union alleges Horizon requires pilots who report fatigue at their home base to travel to another city as passengers before taking the rest provided under their contract.

The union alleges the practice violates the Railway Labor Act and is asking the court to order Horizon to stop it and restore the negotiated rest protections.

“Management cannot pick and choose which parts of our contract it wants to follow,” said Sean Lenney, a Horizon pilot and member of Local 1224, in a news release.

The Teamsters also said Thursday that 99% of pilots who voted backed a no-confidence measure against Carlos Zendejas, Horizon’s senior vice president of operations. The union’s Horizon Air Pilots Executive Council called for his removal following the vote.

Horizon and its pilots have been negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement for more than three and a half years, according to the union. Pilots held informational pickets in Seattle and Boise, Idaho, on Oct. 15 over issues including pay, staffing, and training.

#6155. Amex Gold Card Review: Benefits & Points For Those Who Like To Eat

The American Express® Gold Card is one of the most rewarding cards out there if you’re looking to earn Amex Membership Rewards points.

The Amex Gold Card is an absolute powerhouse if you spend a lot on food, whether it’s at restaurants or supermarkets (or a combination of both). While the card has a somewhat steep annual fee, the good news is that it offers credits that can largely help offset it. We’re also currently seeing an exceptional welcome offer, making it the ideal time to pick up this card. Anyway, enough of an intro, let’s get into my in-depth Amex Gold Card review.

Link: Learn more about the American Express® Gold Card

Before I get into my full Amex Gold Card review, let me summarize some of the most important features:

Here are my thoughts on the major pros and cons of the Amex Gold Card:

For someone looking to earn Membership Rewards points, the Amex Gold Card is one of the most rewarding cards out there. To start, let’s take a look at the welcome offer on the card, along with the eligibility requirements and fees. After all, these are important factors people consider when applying for a card.

The Amex Gold Card has an improved welcome offer: You may be eligible for as high as 100,000 Membership Rewards® Points after spending $8,000 in eligible purchases on your new Card in your first 6 months of Membership. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The way this works, you can apply for the card, and then find out your offer amount. Then you can decide whether you want to accept the offer or not. That’s an unconventional approach for a welcome offer. At least Amex has the “apply with confidence” feature, so there won’t be a hard credit pull unless you accept the offer.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, Membership Rewards points are worth 1.7 cents each. So if you are eligible for a bonus of 100,000 points, those are worth $1,700, by my valuation.

This is a huge bonus, and on top of that, you have a full six months to complete the minimum spending requirement, which should be easy enough for many people to accomplish, as that translates to roughly $1,333 per month in required spending. Personally I’d only apply for the card if I got a welcome offer of at least 60,000 points (or ideally 80,000 points), but everyone has to decide for themselves what they’re willing to “settle” for.

The welcome bonus on the Amex Gold Card isn’t available to those who have or have had the card, or those who have had the Premier Rewards Gold Card in the past. Furthermore, those who have or have had an American Express Platinum Card® (learn more) may also not be eligible for the welcome offer on the card.

However, if you have had one of these cards before, you’re still eligible for the card, but you’re just not eligible for the welcome offer (which is “once in a lifetime”). In some circumstances, it could still be worth getting the card in those situations, if you’d benefit from it on an ongoing basis.

Let me emphasize that you’ll want to apply for the Amex Gold before you apply for the Amex Platinum. That’s because if you have the Amex Gold, you’re still eligible for the Amex Platinum offer, while the inverse isn’t true.

See this post for all the rules on applying for Amex cards, and see this post for details on getting approved for the Amex Gold Card.

The Amex Gold Card has a $325 annual fee. There is no annual fee for up to five additional cards. Meanwhile, the annual fee for six or more additional cards is $35 for each card (Rates & Fees).

Note that Amex Gold Card authorized users don’t receive some of the same benefits as the primary cardmember, but their spending does count toward the rewards that the primary cardmember earns.

The Amex Gold Card has no foreign transaction fees (Rates & Fees), so you can use it for purchases globally. That’s especially useful when you consider that you can earn 4x points on dining abroad, all with no foreign transaction fees.

What makes the Amex Gold Card so valuable is the bonus categories it offers, in the form of Membership Rewards points. The bonus categories include the following:

This is an outstanding return on spending. Based on my valuation of Amex points at 1.7 cents each, that’s like an 8.5% return on eligible prepaid hotel stays, a 6.8% return at restaurants and at U.S. supermarkets, and a 5.1% return on eligible flights.

Now let’s take a closer look at just how those bonus categories are defined.

The Amex Gold Card offers 5x Membership Rewards points on prepaid hotels that are booked through Amex Travel. As a general rule of thumb, this isn’t worth it. That’s because you’re usually not earning loyalty points with your preferred hotel program when you book through Amex Travel, so that’s quite an opportunity cost.

With the Amex Gold Card you’ll earn 4x points on the first $50,000 spent every calendar year at restaurants worldwide, and after that you’ll earn a single point per dollar spent.

Generally speaking, restaurants are defined pretty broadly, and the category includes everything from fast food to cafes to fine dining. This even includes delivery and takeout, given the popularity of that nowadays.

Just note that convenience stores, nightclubs, and restaurants located within other establishments won’t typically qualify for bonus points. Furthermore, eligibility for bonus points is determined based on how the merchant chooses to be categorized. There’s a chance that some merchants may not be categorized as a restaurant, even though you might consider them a restaurant.

For dining, this card even beats the 3x points that the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (learn more) and Chase Sapphire Reserve® (learn more) offer — this is one of the best rewards cards for dining purchases.

The Amex Gold Card offers 4x points on the first $25,000 spent every calendar year at U.S. supermarkets, and after that you’ll earn a single point per dollar. This excludes superstores and warehouse clubs, so don’t expect you’ll be able to earn those bonus points at Sam’s Club, for example. This is one of the best rewards cards for grocery store purchases.

The Amex Gold Card offers 3x points on airfare, with no limits on how many bonus points you can earn. This only applies when booking directly with an airline, through the Amex Travel App™ or through amextravel.com. Furthermore, charter flights and private jet flights are excluded.

Officially, booking through online travel agencies (except Amex Travel) wouldn’t earn you bonus points, though in practice, it may still sometimes code for 3x points. That’s because often online travel agencies still have the airline bill you directly when you book flights through them. This is one of the best rewards cards for airfare purchases.

The Amex Gold Card also offers 2x points on prepaid car rentals and cruises booked through Amex Travel. This bonus category doesn’t make or break the card, but it’s a nice extra, especially if you already make these bookings occasionally.

The Amex Gold Card earns Membership Rewards points. This is one of the major transferable points currencies, and is a favorite points currency for many.

The best way to redeem your Amex points is to transfer them to one of the Membership Rewards airline or hotel partners. Points can be transferred to about 20 partners, consisting primarily of airline loyalty programs, but also of some hotel loyalty programs.

The reason this represents such a good deal is that you can get outsized value toward first and business class travel. These tickets are often disproportionately expensive if paying cash, while they can be a good deal on points. On top of that, Amex often has transfer bonuses, which can stretch your points even further.

While you can redeem Membership Rewards points toward the cost of merchandise or gift cards, or to pay off your statement, these aren’t good uses of your points. You’ll typically get less than 1.0 cent of value per point, so that’s not how I’d redeem them.

In general, I’d recommend earning Membership Rewards points if your primary interest is transferring points to partner programs.

The Amex Gold Card offers a variety of benefits that can help offset the annual fee of the card. In particular, the Amex Gold offers statement credits for eligible purchases, which could save you up to $424 per year, more than offsetting the annual fee. Let’s take a closer look at how these work (Enrollment is required for select benefits).

The first perk is that the Amex Gold Card offers a dining credit of up to $120 per year. There are some restrictions to be aware of with this credit:

The Amex Gold Card offers up to $120 in Uber Cash annually:

This is a fantastic benefit and should be worth face value for anyone who uses Uber at least once a month. Even if you don’t use Uber, this can be useful for getting food delivery through Uber Eats.

The Amex Gold Card offers up to $100 in Resy credits annually:

The Amex Gold Card offers up to $84 in Dunkin’ credits annually:

One thing I’d mention is that anecdotally this also works for Dunkin’ reloads, so you can always get the Dunkin’ app, and then load $7 onto your account each month, and that should trigger the credit. That’s a great way to use this to “bank” credit with Dunkin’ toward a future purchase.

One of the great features of Amex cards is access to Amex Offers, which offers savings or bonus points on purchases with all kinds of retailers. There’s huge value to be had in getting as many Amex cards as possible, so that you can get these offers on multiple cards. Amex Offers could save you hundreds of dollars per year — just note that enrollment is required to take advantage of individual offers.

For staying two or more nights at select luxury hotels, you can receive extra benefits through The Hotel Collection. Benefits include a $100 hotel credit and a room upgrade, if available. This is different than Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts®, which requires having the Amex Platinum Card.

Holding the Amex Gold Card entitles you to a complimentary upgrade to Hertz Five Star status (enrollment required). This gets you an upgrade to a higher car class on rentals when available as well as a 25% bonus on all Hertz rentals. If you already rent cars through Hertz, this is a nice extra. It’s one of the more recently added benefits on the Amex Gold Card, too, since it was introduced in celebration of the card’s 60th anniversary.

The Amex Gold Card comes with a handful of travel insurance benefits that can protect your trip when you pay with your card. Check the card’s benefits guide for exact exclusions and limits, but here’s a quick overview:

Up to $300 per Covered Trip that is delayed for more than 12 hours; and 2 claims per Eligible Card per 12 consecutive month period. Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by New Hampshire Insurance Company, an AIG Company. Baggage insurance plan: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car rental loss and damage insurance: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car Rental Loss or Damage Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc.

The Amex Gold Card is a great card for anyone who spends a lot of money on food (whether at restaurants or supermarkets), and who is looking to earn Membership Rewards points. Furthermore, the card potentially offers over $400 in annual credits, between the dining credit, Resy credit, Dunkin’ credit, and Uber Cash.

I’d argue that if you value earning Membership Rewards points, if you spend a lot on dining, and if you can use a decent number of the card’s credits, then picking up this card is a slam dunk. It’s hard to beat this kind of return on dining and supermarket spending, and it’s a great complement to some other Amex cards.

The great welcome offer that’s available is the icing on the cake, and makes applying for the card all the more tempting. I’d recommend confirming you’re eligible for a welcome bonus on the higher end of the spectrum with the current offer of as high as 100,000 points, especially because you can only get an Amex Gold Card welcome bonus once.

I will say, the Amex Gold Card might not be for you if you don’t spend a lot on dining, if you don’t live in a major city where you can easily use the credits, if you value airport lounge access as a card perk, or if you’d rather earn cash back than travel rewards, since those are all potential considerations with the card.

It’s also worth comparing the Amex Gold Card to other options. Here’s how the Amex Gold Card stacks up against some of the most popular alternatives.

The Amex Platinum Card (learn more) has a higher annual fee than the Amex Gold and comes with many more perks and annual credits. Here are the biggest differences to know about:

If you travel many times a year and want as many benefits as possible, the Amex Platinum Card is hard to beat. That said, the Amex Gold Card still offers a better return on spending when it comes to dining out and shopping at U.S. supermarkets. As I see it, the cards serve different purposes — one is about the perks, and the other is about the return on spending.

If you’re looking for a rewards card with a lower annual fee, the Chase Sapphire Preferred Card (learn more) is worth comparing against the Amex Gold Card as well. It has a much lower annual fee of $95 and fewer perks, but it still earns very strong rewards:

Between the Amex Gold Card and the Chase Sapphire Preferred, the best option for you could come down to whether you prefer Amex Membership Rewards points or Chase Ultimate Rewards points. Make sure to compare your welcome bonus offers between both cards before making a final decision as well.

The Citi Strata Premier® Card (learn more) is another great rewards card with useful bonus categories at the $95 annual fee level:

If you want just one rewards card in your wallet, the Citi Strata Premier makes a strong case for itself with its bonus categories. I value both Amex points and Citi ThankYou points at 1.7 cents apiece, but some travelers might prefer one rewards program over the other depending on their favorite airline and hotel partners.

The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card (learn more) is one of my favorite cards for those looking for a simple strategy, and who don’t want to focus on a bunch of credits, maximizing bonus categories, etc.

The card has a $95 annual fee, and offers a minimum of 2x miles per dollar spent, making this one of the best cards for everyday spending. The reasonable annual fee plus the flat 2x miles is ideal for someone who doesn’t maybe spend a huge amount in categories that are otherwise eligible for bonus points.

The Amex Gold Card is one of American Express’ best rewards cards for earning points. With 4x points on dining and supermarkets, earning Membership Rewards points is easy.

The card also offers some credits that are potentially useful, which for many will help offset the annual fee. The card offers up to $120 dining credits, up to $120 in Uber Cash annually, up to $100 in Resy credits annually, and up to $84 in Dunkin’ credits annually — a total of $424 in annual credits if you take advantage of all of them. If you don’t yet have the card, it’s seriously worth considering.

#6154. Democrat poised to flip deep-red House seat without airing a single TV ad

Fox News contributor Guy Benson breaks down the GOP midterm losses, including Vice President JD Vance's social media post on the impact of the Iran conflict on voters.

Two years after losing to Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais by 43 points, Democrat Victoria Broderick is leading in his deep-red Tennessee district by just 280 votes in the state’s unofficial final results — despite spending under $100,000 and airing no paid TV ads.

If her lead holds, the result would end DesJarlais’ 16-year congressional career. First elected in 2010, the Republican was seeking his ninth term in a district President Donald Trump carried by 24 points in 2024.

The latest FEC figures available before Election Day show DesJarlais’ campaign spent $508,166 through Oct. 14, compared with just $90,062 for Broderick. His campaign also raised more than seven times as much as hers — $667,181 to $94,217 — yet the longtime incumbent is trailing in the deep-red seat.

REDISTRICTING EFFORTS BLOW UP IN REPUBLICANS' FACES AMID HISTORIC HOUSE LOSSES

Broderick holds a narrow lead over DesJarlais in Tennessee’s 4th Congressional District after running a low-cost campaign focused on grassroots organizing. (Victoria4Tennessee)

Axios reported, citing AdImpact, that Broderick’s campaign had no record of airing paid television ads. Instead, she credited a grassroots operation that had been building for more than two years.

Broderick was not the only Democrat threatening to pull off a low-dollar House upset. Axios also highlighted a similar race in North Carolina, where High Point Mayor Cyril Jefferson currently leads Republican Rep. Addison McDowell 51.1% to 48.9%.

Axios reported, citing AdImpact, that Jefferson had no tracked advertising spending, although a separate tracker lists $2,000 in Google ads, including YouTube placements.

LEE CARTER: THE 5 WORDS THAT EXPLAIN THIS ELECTION BETTER THAN ANY COMMERCIAL

McDowell had won the district by 38.3 points in 2024, according to election results.

High Point Mayor, North Carolina Mayor Cyril Jefferson leads Republican Rep. Addison McDowell in North Carolina’s 6th Congressional District (Cyril for Congress)

Broderick told Axios that her apparent upset was not a surprise to her team.

"I know it was a shock for the rest of the country, but it wasn’t a shock for our team," she said.

Jefferson similarly credited volunteers, saying, "You have to go engage them."

Rep. Addison McDowell, R-N.C., and Rep. Scott DesJarlais, R-Tenn., trail Democratic challengers who ran campaigns with little or no paid television advertising. (Getty Images)

Wake Forest University political science professor John Dinan told local news outlet WFDD that challengers in such a Republican-leaning district would normally need "a lot of TV ads and a lot of money," but "there wasn’t a whole lot of money spent."

The two races showed how grassroots organizing and strong local candidates can make traditionally Republican districts competitive despite major financial disadvantages.

Editor's Note: This story has been updated to reflect that the Associated Press has not yet called either race.

Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

#6153. House conservative emerges with 2028 presidential pick after GOP's midterm massacre: 'I am all in'

Secretary of State Marco Rubio looks on during a dedication ceremony for an annex building at the U.S. embassy in New Delhi on May 23, 2026. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AFP)

One of the original members of the House Freedom Caucus has made his decision on who to support in 2028 after Republicans' historic losses in Tuesday night's midterms.

Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., told Fox News Digital "I am all in" for Secretary of State Marco Rubio and called on fellow Republicans to begin thinking about how to rebuild in the wake of their election losses.

FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM'

He also told Fox News Digital that Republicans "have to do better at communicating" since they "can't push policy" after losing the House and Senate majorities.

Among those communication changes, he suggested changing the way Republicans discuss immigration.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

"We need to get off the deportation messages, take credit for closing the border, and now start finding a path forward for those here illegally obeying the laws," Stutzman said. "No citizenship just work visas."

A blue tsunami swept both federal and state races on Tuesday night. In the House, both battleground districts and seats considered safe GOP strongholds saw upset Democrat victories.

Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., attends a House Financial Services Committee hearing on May 7, 2025. (CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

Dozens of races have yet to be called, but Democrats are projected to hold at least 54 seats in the Senate. In the House so far, they're projected to win 240 seats, compared to 147 projected for Republicans.

Democrats also scored upset victories in multiple governorships, namely in Texas and Iowa.

FROM TEXAS TO KANSAS, 6 STUNNING MIDTERM RESULTS THAT UPENDED THE POLITICAL MAP

And within hours of the writing landing on the wall, various GOP factions began publicly discussing how to rebuild and move forward.

Vice President JD Vance quickly distanced himself from the war in Iran, which is thought to be one of the biggest drivers of voters moving away from the GOP.

TRUMP TOLD DONORS 'WE NEED TO ELECT JD,' SOURCE CONFIRMS, AS HE WEIGHS VANCE OR RUBIO IN 2028

Vice President JD Vance speaks at a campaign rally at Griffiss International Airport on Nov. 2, 2026, in Rome, New York. (Tom Brenner/Getty Images)

"The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance posted on X in a lengthy statement. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

Vance is considered a top presidential contender for Republicans in 2028, as is Rubio.

But it's not clear yet whether their senior roles in the Trump administration will similarly sandbag their prospective bids.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

#6152. Defiant Ritz-Carlton Singapore Joining Marriott Bonvoy… Finally!

The world’s only Ritz-Carlton that doesn’t participate in the Marriott Bonvoy program will finally be joining, which seems long overdue. I can’t imagine the hotel will be particularly generous, but we’ll see!

The 608-key Ritz-Carlton Millenia Singapore will be joining the Marriott Bonvoy program as of December 1, 2026. So as of that date, Bonvoy members will be able to earn and redeem points, and take advantage of Bonvoy elite perks, when staying at the hotel (admittedly Bonvoy elite perks at Ritz-Carlton properties are fairly limited, as breakfast isn’t a benefit for any elite tier).

As I covered in late 2025, this property is the only Ritz-Carlton in the world that doesn’t participate in the Bonvoy program. The backstory here is that the hotel opened back in 1996, and at the time, Ritz-Carlton didn’t have any sort of a loyalty program that awarded points.

In 2010, the Ritz-Carlton Rewards program started awarding points for hotel stays, as a parallel program to Marriott Rewards. The ability to earn and redeem points came at a cost to individual hotels, but it was intended to boost occupancy and average daily rates.

Initially, hotels had the option of whether they wanted to opt in or out of the program. Most hotels bought into the concept, though the Ritz-Carlton Osaka and Ritz-Carlton Singapore were the two hotels that opted out. The Ritz-Carlton Osaka eventually decided to participate, leaving the Ritz-Carlton Singapore as the only hotel that’s not participating.

Ultimately when the Marriott Bonvoy program formed as the combination of Marriott Rewards and Starwood Preferred Guest, the hotel could still stick to its legacy contract of not having to participate in the program. Clearly the owners of the hotel have now had a change of heart… or something!

Obviously we don’t have any sort of an official explanation for the reason that this Ritz-Carlton property is finally backtracking. I can’t imagine that Marriott gave the owners an ultimatum, given that Marriott is known for letting hotel owners get away with anything, as long as they get paid.

My guess is that the competitive realities just finally caught up with this hotel — Singapore is an increasingly competitive hotel market, this is a massive hotel with 600+ rooms to fill every night, and the hotel is also a bit past its prime.

The truth is that loyalty programs exist for a reason, as they’re a great tool for getting heads into beds. Obviously the hotel will be on the hook for some additional loyalty fees, but I imagine this will make the hotel more appealing to people who otherwise wouldn’t have considered it.

I also have to imagine that even though the hotel did a decent job communicating its lack of participation in Marriott Bonvoy, I still suspect many guests didn’t realize this, and ended up being disappointed.

As of December 1, 2026, the Ritz-Carlton Singapore will be joining the Marriott Bonvoy program. This is the only Ritz-Carlton hotel in the world that hasn’t participated in Bonvoy, so this is great to see.

The backstory is that the hotel opened before Ritz-Carlton had a loyalty program, and then when a program was finally formed, participation was optional. Literally every other Ritz-Carlton in the world saw value in this… except this one, apparently.

Fortunately they’ve now come to their senses, or something, so it’s great to see that this will be changing.

What do you make of the Ritz-Carlton Singapore joining Bonvoy?

Amazon has a new restaurant delivery partner for its Prime members: Uber Eats, which replaces the Grubhub+ benefit Prime members had until today.

To celebrate the new partnership, Amazon Prime members can get $20 off each of their first two eligible Uber Eats orders of $25 or more on linked accounts made via Amazon, as long as those orders are for U.S. restaurants and placed by Nov. 18.

Beyond the limited-time launch promotion, Prime members will get $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats orders of $25 or more placed through the Amazon app or website. Interestingly, this appears to work separately from any existing Uber Eats account or benefits you may already have.

Related: Which is the best food delivery app?

There's no need to download another app or create a separate Uber Eats account to use this perk. When you opt in through Amazon, you can use your existing Prime account information, including linked payment methods.

Think of it almost like ordering a box of paper towels from Amazon with free Prime delivery, only this time it's a salad, burger, breakfast tacos or fries. You place the order via Uber Eats in your Amazon account, almost as you would any other Prime delivery, but this time it is fulfilled by Uber Eats instead of your friendly neighborhood Amazon delivery truck.

Amazon has also said that there will be additional Prime-exclusive offers available only on Amazon that could save you more than $175 per year, so we'll be sure to keep an eye out for those.

TPG tip: Amazon Prime Visa cardmembers earn 5% back on all Uber Eats orders through Dec. 5, 2026 with eligible Prime membership.

The information for the Prime Visa has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

This $20 introductory promo seems to apply whether you use pickup or delivery, which isn't always the case with Uber Eats promos. So, it is possible to truly save $20 on a $25 order if you select pickup. If you opt for delivery, you will likely have some service fees and a tip to factor into the equation.

One thing to remember: After the introductory promotion ends, you may want to compare the total cost of ordering through the Amazon-linked version of Uber Eats with any promotions, credit card benefits or discounts available through your regular Uber Eats account. The best deal may depend on which version of Uber Eats you're using.

#6149. American Airlines Quietly Removes Trump From West Palm Beach Gate Monitors

American Airlines has updated the gate monitors for flights to West Palm Beach, and they no longer mention President Trump. This seems like a sensible change (unrelated to politics), and the timing sure is… interesting.

Over the summer, we saw Palm Beach International Airport (PBI) renamed President Donald J. Trump International Airport. We knew that Trump wanted an airport named after him, and some conservative politicians in Florida came together to make it happen.

It’s interesting to see how airlines handled this. At the time, American updated its gate monitors for flights to West Palm Beach. The monitors initially read “West Palm Beach, FL.” American then updated the monitors to say “Pres DJT, W Palm Beach.” Now JonNYC reports that as of this week, the airport name listed on the monitors has been changed again, and is back to the original name, with no mention of Trump.

so… has anyone noticed that AA has changed the gate monitors from “Pres DJT, W Palm Beach” back to “West Palm Beach, FL” ? https://t.co/IG2mPA3zgG

JonNYC specifically emphasizes that he’s not claiming there’s any connection between this and the election results, though the timing of it happening this week sure is interesting.

Personally I’m not a fan of airports being named after even semi-controversial figures, and particularly politicians. It’s something I’ve said over and over, regardless of the party affiliation of the person. Unless a city has multiple airports, I think it’s also stupid to identify the airport based on the name rather than the place.

Like, it makes sense to clarify London Heathrow (LHR) vs. London Gatwick (LGW), but it’s not like there are multiple airports in West Palm Beach. For that matter, saying you’re “flying to President Trump” just sounds a little weird, in my opinion.

JonNYC notes that he’s not suggesting that this had anything to do with the recent election, though everything about the timing here is interesting:

American Airlines CEO Robert Isom: "From a commercial aviation perspective, the eyes of the world have been on us, and we've certainly delivered… No doubt, it's a result of the economy and the job market." https://t.co/28JzoEf4Z3 pic.twitter.com/BcgYJbChNz

American Airlines seems to have quietly reversed course on how it refers to West Palm Beach’s airport on its gate monitors. In recent months, the airline has referred to the airport as “Pres DJT, W Palm Beach,” while now it seems to be back to “West Palm Beach, FL.”

This change comes the same week as the midterm elections, though everyone can decide for themselves to what extent these points are related…

What do you make of this American gate monitor change?

#6148. Alito reiterates he's not retiring, is committed through end of current Supreme Court term

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis warns that an incoming Democratic Senate majority means no Supreme Court Justice or major cabinet officials will be confirmed.

Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito confirmed to Fox News that he has no plans to retire and is committed through at least the current term, which is set to end in late June.

Alito made the statement Thursday amid speculation about the future of the Supreme Court after a disastrous GOP performance in the midterm elections.

When the new congressional term begins in January, Democrats will be in firm control of the Senate, with predictions, including from Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, that this will not change for at least six years. That would make it extremely difficult, if not impossible, for President Donald Trump to fill any potential vacancy with a conservative after this year.

ALITO NOT EXPECTED TO RETIRE THIS TERM, COOLING SUPREME COURT VACANCY SPECULATION: SOURCES

United States Supreme Court Associate Justice Samuel Alito on October 7, 2022, in Washington, D.C. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

After Justice Clarence Thomas, 78, Alito is the oldest member of the Supreme Court at 76 years old.

"Chance of confirming a worthy successor to Justice Thomas and/or Alito during President Trump’s term: Zero. Chance of confirming a worthy successor during a hypothetical GOP admin 2029-2033: probably zero (GOP won’t be able to recapture enough seats in 28)," DeSantis posted to X on Tuesday night.

REPUBLICANS SOUND ALARM OVER HIDDEN MIDTERM STAKES THAT COULD RESHAPE SUPREME COURT FOR DECADES

"Assuming Republicans lose the seats where prediction markets have the Democrats at 90+% to win, that would produce 55 Democrat Senate seats," DeSantis added.

JONATHAN TURLEY: SHERROD BROWN'S PLEDGE TURNS ADVICE AND CONSENT INTO A PUNCHLINE

Supreme Court Associate Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas wait to leave the stage after the inauguration ceremonies in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 20, 2025. (Chip Somodevilla/AFP via Getty Images)

DEMS SEIZE THE SENATE AS BLUE TIDAL WAVE CRASHES DEEP INTO TRUMP COUNTRY, TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLDS

Ed Whelan, a conservative legal expert who clerked for the late Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia, wrote on X that Trump is now effectively blocked from appointing federal judges or Supreme Court justices during the final two years of his term.

"If a Republican is elected president in 2028, that president will not be able to appoint any justices or judges until Republicans regain the Senate," Whelan wrote. "Given the deep hole, that might not happen until 2033. "

The Supreme Court is seen on Friday, Feb. 20, 2026. (Annabelle Gordon/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Whelan also explained that a justice resigning during the upcoming "lame duck" session is highly unlikely and Republicans would have a hard time securing 51 votes.

"If Sherrod Brown wins Ohio seat, he gets sworn into Senate in early December, so Senate becomes 52R-48D," Whelan wrote. "Collins and Murkowski would be unlikely to support anyone Trump would nominate. John Cornyn, Thom Tillis, and Bill Cassidy aren’t going to be eager to do Trump any favors. And there are other senators—e.g., John Curtis of Utah—who would be leery of anyone Trump would be eager to push through."

Fox News' Andrew Mark Miller contributed to this report.

#6147. Avelo Airlines Cancels All 6 International Routes: See Full List Now

Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America. Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand. His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

Avelo Airlines cut all of its international routes from its network this year, as the airline redeploys its aircraft on domestic routes instead. The airline is a Texas-based ultra-low-cost carrier that has evolved from Xtra Airways and Casino Express Airlines. The carrier, which has a growing number of flights on the US East Coast, has had terrible luck with international services.

Indeed, one just lasted a matter of weeks. All international flights operated by the airline were terminated in January of this year. Many of these routes faced no direct competition.

Being a budget carrier, Avelo offers a basic economy service with extra ancillary services like checked baggage, meals onboard or seat selection coming for a fee. The airline has focused on serving secondary airports, or routes that face no competition. As such, the airline tried its hand in international flying. However, this chapter was ultimately short-lived.

Of its six international routes, three of these were served from Bradley International Airport (BDL), which serves Hartford, Connecticut. A sole international route operated from Wilmington International Airport (ILM) in North Carolina, and the remaining two services were from Raleigh–Durham International Airport (RDU). Their destinations were popular tourist hotspots in the Caribbean.

Avelo's decision to cancel all international services came as part of a major restructuring of the airline's network. It refocused on a back-to-basics domestic strategy after financial losses and fleet changes.

Avelo began operating two international services from Hartford in November 2024, with the airline connecting the city to Cancun International Airport (CUN) and Montego Bay (MBJ). This was quickly followed by a link to the Dominican Republic in February 2025. These were the airline's first regular scheduled international services.

Raleigh joined the pack in February of the same year, with two international services operating to Montego Bay and Punta Cana. These operated for almost a year, before the airline's ultimate termination of all international flying.

Wilmington (ILM) saw its sole international link to Punta Cana go live in December. However, after just a number of short weeks, the airline pulled its aircraft from the route, citing weaker-than-expected demand, and Wilmington lost its sole international route.

Seasonal and year round frequencies are trimmed, forcing travelers to reroute through neighboring airports for connections.

Data from Cirium, an aviation analytics company, clearly identifies the painfully low load factors that Avelo faced when operating international flights. Airlines aim for a minimum 80% load factor, which provides enough income to allow the flight to operate at a profit.

Since the airline first launched into international flying, load factors only steadily increased to around 79% in June 2025 before dipping again on the other side of the busy summer travel period. After Avelo's swift exit from international flying, the carrier is now focused on scaling up a number of core domestic bases and has no immediate plans to return to the international skies.

One of my favorite things about World of Hyatt points is how much flexibility they offer. You could redeem just a few thousand points for a night at a Category 1 Hyatt hotel or use a larger stash to book a higher-category hotel or all-inclusive resort.

Since Hyatt still uses award charts for most of its properties, you can sometimes get outsize value by redeeming points when cash rates are high. But free nights aren't the only way to use your points. From room upgrades and dining experiences to airline miles and rental cars, here's how you can redeem World of Hyatt points, including which options offer the best value.

The best way to redeem Hyatt points is usually for free hotel nights. Hyatt has award charts for most free night awards, though some are dynamically priced. There are also ways to combine points with cash and free night certificates.

Hyatt publishes award charts for free night awards at Hyatt hotels and resorts, participating resorts within the Hyatt Inclusive Collection brands and Miraval resorts. Each of these charts has five award pricing tiers — Lowest, Low, Moderate, Upper and Top — for each category.

Here's the award chart for standard room award nights at Hyatt hotels and resorts.

Hyatt publishes separate award charts for Hyatt Inclusive Collection brands and Miraval resorts, as well as for club rooms, standard suites and premium suites. Check out our guide to the Hyatt award charts for all the charts.

You can click on "Points Calendar" on the results page for any particular property when searching for award stays to see how many points each night costs.

However, free night awards at Mr & Mrs Smith hotels and Homes & Hideaways by World of Hyatt are priced dynamically based on paid rates. For example, this night at a Homes & Hideaways property in Florida would cost 16,011 points or $192.13. This means you'd get 1.2 cents per point when redeeming Hyatt points for this night.

And this night at a Mr & Mrs Smith property in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, would cost 8,750 points or $58.91. This means you'd only get 0.67 cents per point when redeeming Hyatt points for this night.

TPG's November 2026 valuations peg Hyatt points at 1.65 cents each. As such, you'll generally want to get at least this much value when redeeming your Hyatt points.

Related: Best Hyatt hotels in the world to book with points

You can also book Points + Cash rates for some stays. When these rates are available for your chosen room type and property, you'll redeem 50% of the points required for a free night and get 50% to 70% off the standard rate (which may be higher than the best available rate).

For example, I could redeem 12,000 points, book a Points + Cash rate of 6,000 points plus $156.50 or book a paid rate of $220.16 for this night at the Hyatt Centric Rittenhouse Square Philadelphia.

When redeeming points, I'd get 1.83 cents per point. And when booking a Points + Cash rate, I'd get 1.06 cents per point.

Related: Which credit card should you use for Hyatt stays?

You can also combine Hyatt points with paid nights and even free night certificates when booking with the Hyatt Pay My Way feature. To use this feature, sign in to your Hyatt account, search for a paid stay, click on the property and room type of your choice and then click on rates until you see one with a Pay My Way option.

Click on the Pay My Way box, and then you can choose whether to use points, cash, Points + Cash or free night certificates for each night.

I often use Pay My Way when redeeming free night certificates, as this lets me book a multinight stay even if I only have one free night certificate. I've also used Pay My Way to redeem points for a stay with one particularly expensive night.

Related: The best Hyatt Category 4 hotels to maximize your free night award certificates

You can redeem points to upgrade eligible paid stays at many Hyatt hotels and resorts. Here's a look at the upgrade rate per night:

You can sometimes redeem points for an upgrade at the time of booking. In the following example, you could redeem 9,500 points for a premium suite free night, 4,750 points plus $158 for a premium suite Points + Cash booking or 9,000 points plus $152 to upgrade a paid night to a premium suite.

If you don't upgrade at the time of booking, you can call (800) 544-9288 in the U.S. and Canada or contact a Global Care Center to see if your existing stay is eligible for an upgrade with points.

Related: Your ultimate guide to Hyatt hotel brands

You can redeem Hyatt points for dining and spa experiences at participating locations even if you aren't spending the night. Plus, you can redeem points during stays at participating locations to pay for in-room movies, parking, transportation and more.

To redeem points, simply request to use Hyatt points at checkout and choose how many points to redeem. You should be able to redeem points at participating locations based on the following chart:

As you can see, the redemption rate you'll get ranges from 1 to 1.54 cents per point, which is below TPG's November 2026 valuation of 1.65 cents per point for Hyatt points. As such, you'll usually want to find higher-value ways to redeem your Hyatt points.

You can redeem Hyatt points for Find experiences. For example, you could pay $60 plus taxes or redeem 4,286 points for this one-hour aerial yoga and meditation class.

Or, you could redeem 5,357 points or pay $75 plus taxes for an e-bike tour of San Diego.

It's worth taking a look at Find experiences, especially if you select Find experience credits as Hyatt Milestone Rewards. But you usually won't get outsize value when redeeming points for these experiences.

Related: Why bidding on a Hyatt Find experience auction might be the most valuable way to redeem your World of Hyatt points

You can convert Hyatt points into airline miles with the following programs:

For most of the airline programs, you'll get 1 mile for every 2.5 Hyatt points you convert. However, Hyatt uses different conversion rates for Aeromexico Rewards, Air China PhoenixMiles, China Eastern Miles, Qantas Frequent Flyer, Southwest Rapid Rewards and Virgin Atlantic Flying Club.

You must convert at least 5,000 points at a time but can convert additional points in increments of 1,250. If you convert 50,000 points or more, you'll usually get an extra 5,000 bonus miles.

However, converting Hyatt points to airline miles will rarely make sense. Conversions can take six to eight weeks. Plus, at the usual 2.5:1 conversion ratio, transferring 5,000 Hyatt points yields 2,000 airline miles. Based on TPG's November 2026 valuations, you'd be giving up approximately $82.50 in Hyatt points for those 2,000 miles.

You can redeem Hyatt points for Avis free day awards, which are valid at participating locations in the U.S. and Canada, by calling (800) 544-9288. When available, you can redeem 6,000 points per day for an intermediate-size car. However, there are blackout periods that you'll see on the redemption certificate once you redeem your points. Avis free day awards usually expire one year after they're issued.

World of Hyatt members can redeem points for an Aeroplan flight reward certificate valid on Air Canada flights. The 30,000-point certificate costs 50,000 Hyatt points, and you can apply it toward the base fare in points of an Aeroplan flight reward.

Given that TPG's November 2026 valuations peg Hyatt points at 1.65 cents each and Aeroplan points at 1.45 cents each, this won't be a good-value redemption for most travelers. However, if you were planning to convert Hyatt points to Aeroplan points, the flight reward certificate might provide better value.

Related: How to redeem Aeroplan points for maximum value

World of Hyatt and American Airlines AAdvantage are winding down their partnership. But eligible Explorist and Globalist members can redeem Hyatt points for AAdvantage Status for a Day until 1 a.m. EST on Nov. 16.

You can redeem 5,000 Hyatt points to get AAdvantage Gold status for a day, 8,000 points to get AAdvantage Platinum status for a day and 12,000 points to get AAdvantage Platinum Pro status for a day.

However, you can only use these awards on your own travel itineraries, and some fares aren't eligible.

Related: Why I rely on credit cards to earn American Airlines elite status

Finally, you can redeem Hyatt points for a future meeting credit to use for meetings and catered events at participating Hyatt hotels and resorts based on the following chart:

As you can see, the redemption rate is 1.33 cents per point regardless of how many points you redeem toward a future meeting credit. You must call a Hyatt Global Care Center to redeem points for a future meeting credit. You can't use future meeting credits at Hyatt Vacation Club, Bahia Principe and Destination by Hyatt Residences locations.

Redeeming World of Hyatt points for free nights is usually the best way to get good value from your points. I particularly like redeeming Hyatt points at hotels where cash rates are high, as I can often get outsize value. But I'll also redeem points on stays with resort fees, as Hyatt waives resort fees on free night awards.

Other redemption options, including room upgrades, Find experiences and airline miles, can make sense in certain situations. But I generally recommend saving your Hyatt points for free night awards, especially if you can be flexible about where and when you stay.

#6145. KLM Plans 15% Workforce Reduction And Simpler Fleet: “Future Not Guaranteed”

It’s obviously a tough time for aviation in general, given the impact of high jet fuel prices. For that matter, Dutch national carrier KLM has faced its own unique challenges, given increasing limits placed on the carrier’s Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS) hub, plus all the competitive challenges (increased competition from regional low cost carriers, Gulf carriers, etc.).

In recent years, we’ve seen KLM introduce initiatives intended to improve economics. The airline is now taking that to the next level, and has just announced an absolutely massive project intended to improve economics by €1 billion per year.

KLM has unveiled the details of a project that it expects will contribute to annual earnings improvements of €1 billion per year, which it hopes will allow the company to invest in fleet, customer experience, and people.

KLM’s plan is to focus on its core strengths, which it describes as a global network of 160 destinations served nonstop from Schiphol, and reliable operations supported by a modern fleet. The company wants to become a smaller, simpler, and more agile organization, through restructuring, outsourcing, and closer collaboration with Air France-KLM.

Here’s how KLM CEO Marjan Rintel describes this initiative:

“Every day, we all work with incredible dedication, commitment, and pride. But KLM’s future is not guaranteed. The environment we operate in is becoming increasingly complex, with global instability, high fuel prices, and growing pressure on the aviation industry. That’s why, at this pivotal moment for KLM, we’re taking far-reaching, sometimes painful measures. Every department and every division will be asked to contribute.”

“We’re doing this with a clear vision for the future: one where KLM remains a great airline that connects customers to the world, a company people want to work for, and one the Netherlands can be proud of.”

How does KLM plan on improving economics by so much over the coming years? For one, the airline will simplify its fleet.

The long term plan is to have a fleet of 185 Airbus, Boeing, and Embraer aircraft. The latest changes particularly center around the European network, where just about all network carriers in Europe struggle to make money, given the costs and competitive landscape.

KLM plans to change the balance between larger and smaller aircraft on European routes. In the long run, the airline will fly a mix of 227-seat Airbus A321neos and 132-seat Embraer E195-E2s. The company no longer plans to acquire Airbus A320neos, which were part of a larger Air France-KLM order, as those planes are instead going to Transavia. Furthermore, in the coming years, we’ll see Boeing 737s and Embraer E190s retired.

Next, the airline hopes to achieve greater flexibility, higher productive, and lower costs, with its labor agreements. As you’d expect, this will be the most painful change. For one, KLM plans to reduce its workforce by around 15%, meaning that around 5,000 positions will be “reorganized.”

This follows the company’s number of staff already declining in recent years. The good news is that there aren’t expected to be mass layoffs — KLM expects to limit the impact on employees through natural attrition, voluntary arrangements, and transfers to other positions.

The airline also emphasizes that employment terms and conditions need to become simpler and more competitive, noting that “continuing on the current path is not sustainable.” KLM wants to work with unions to establish new collective labor agreements, and the company aims to achieve a structural productivity increase of at least 8% by 2028.

This decrease in headcount will come through a combination of Air France and KLM cooperating more closely, outsourcing catering and maintenance, and reducing planned growth of the fleet.

The airline industry is tough in the first place, and among the major network carriers, KLM is perhaps in the toughest spot, when you consider the overall industry dynamics:

KLM is planning to majorly cut costs and simplify things, which is probably necessary in light of how the situation has evolved.

As part of this, the carrier’s short haul fleet will eventually consist of just Airbus A321neos and Embraer E195-E2s. On top of that, we’ll see the airline reduce its workforce by around 15%, through a combination of increasing efficiency, outsourcing jobs, and more. The company will also be looking for some concessions from existing employees.

In total, the company hopes that these changes will contribute €1 billion per year. While aviation is tough across the board, it’s especially tough to be KLM, where you’re reliant on one hub (which regulators keep trying to shrink) with very high costs, and that hub isn’t a market that’s as lucrative as somewhere like London, Paris, etc. I’m a fan of KLM, and I hope these changes don’t do too much to change the quirky spirit of the airline.

What do you make of these major KLM changes?
